3 OBJECTIVES: At the end of this lesson; students should be able to: 1. Identify different types of pattern. 2. Highlight different ways of putting designs together using various elements. 3. Describe the term pattern and Design. 4. Explain the term motif. PATTERNS Pattern is the arrangement of regular and repeated motif from nature or the environment in such a way that rhythm is created in colour, tone or texture on a given surface. Pattern making features very well in textile design, wall papers, wrappers, carpets, boarder designs e.t.c. MOTIF Motif is the unit of design or major theme in an art work especially in pattern making, where it is repeated several times and at regular intervals. Motif can be formed from natural or artificial objects, abstract, geometric, regular or irregular shapes. DESIGN Design is an arrangement or composition of some art elements, motifs, and symbols into a unified piece or pattern. Design has some elements which if well utilized will enhance design making. They include; line, form, color, texture, shape and space. There are different ways of putting designs together using various elements and they include; 1. Pattern making with lines. 2. Design symbols and shapes

7 CROCHETINGWEEK 3: OBJECTIVES: At the end of this lesson; students should be able to: 1.Identify different crochets products. 2.Highlight the materials/tools needed in crocheting. 3.Explain the term crocheting. Crocheting is a process of creating fabric by interlocking loops of yarn, thread, or strands of other materials using a crochet hook. The name is derived from the French term "crochet", meaning small hook. These are made of materials such as metal, wood, or plastic and are manufactured commercially and produced in artisan workshops. The salient difference between crochet and knitting, beyond the implements used for their production, is that each stitch in crochet is completed before proceeding with the next one, while knitting keeps a large number of stitches open at a time. (Variant forms such as Tunisian crochet and broomstick lace keep multiple crochet stitches open at a time.) MATERIALS/TOOLS • Yarn or Thread • Crochet Hooks • Tape Measure • Yarn Needles

11 PAPIER MACHEWEEK 5: OBJECTIVES: At the end of this lesson; students should be able to: 1.Identify the materials/tools needed in Paper Mache. 2.Highlight the procedures involved in Paper Mache. 3.Describe the term Paper Mache. CONTENT The word papier mache which means mashed paper is derived from a French vocabulary. Papier mache can be achieved by boiling paper into a soft mass and mixing it up with an adhesive to stiffen it. It could then be used for making three dimensional objects or vessels such as a tea cup, a bowl etc. This method could actually be adapted by soaking paper in water overnight instead of boiling it. Soaking softens the paper shreds which are afterwards pounded or mashed into pulp. The mass is then mixed with an adhesive (starch) to stiffen it later. MATERIALS 1 Newspaper, toilet paper or any absorbent paper. 2 Cassava starch/adhesive 3 A pair of Scissors 4 A Container for mixing paste 5 A smooth bowl to be used as a mould 6 Lubricant (Vaseline, grease, cream or groundnut oil) 7 Paint (water colour, poster colour etc.) or spray paint.

PROCEDURE • Get your materials/tools. • Soak your absorbent paper in water for at least two days. • Get rid of excess water and pound your soaked paper into a pulp.

13 • Mixed up the paper pulp with cassava starch or glue (top bond) • Lubricate the already made vessel (a cup) to be used with grease, groundnut oil or hair cream. • Apply the paper pulp all over the lubricated vessel in an evenly manner. • Put the paper pulp under the sun to get dry. • Separate the cup (mould) from the dried paper pulp. ASSIGNMENT Produce a vessel or an object of your choice in papier mache.

18 WEEK 9: TIE AND DYE OBJECTIVES: At the end of this lesson; students should be able to: 1. Identify materials needed in the production of tie-dye. 2. Highlight method of production in tie-die. 3. Outline the six materials used in tie- dye. 4. Describe the circling method of tying. 5. Define tie and dye. CONTENT Tie and dye is the method of tying or stitching fabric together to prevent the absorption of dye. The part of the fabric that is tied or stitched disallows the penetration of dye into the fabric (resist technique), hence, a designed is formed. Adire is the name given to indigo dyed cloth (tie- dye) produced by Yoruba women of south western Nigeria using a variety of resist dye techniques. Adire translates as tie and dye, and the earliest cloths were probably simple tied designs on locally-woven hand-spun cotton cloth Adire soon became a major local craft in the towns of Abeokuta and Ibadan. This tied-resist cloth is usually known as "kampala," though a few people still call this adire. Materials needed in the production of tie- dye. • Cotton material • Raffia or twine • Pebbles • Buttons • Scissors

19 • Water • Container • Dye • Salt • Long stick for stirring • Rubber glove • Hydrosulphite • Caustic soda. Method of production. This can be prepared either with hot water or cold water. • Wash and iron material to be dyed. • Tie the cloth to desired pattern. • Put on your rubber glove • Mix your dye solution and chemicals in a container. Dissolve 4 tablespoon full of salt, hydrosulphite and caustic soda in water. • Immerse you fabric into the dye solution and stir for about one hour occasionally. • Remove from the dye and rinse fabric until the water is clean. • Dry and iron the fabric.
